newsitem.title: UK: Third quarter gold demand slips from 1995 record.
newsitem.headline: Third quarter gold demand slips from 1995 record.

text.p: Gold demand in markets monitored by the World Gold Council (WGC) totalled 655 tonnes during the third quarter, two percent off the record 668 tonnes recorded in the same period last year, the WGC said on Wednesday.
In Europe, the United States and Japan gold consumption fell seven percent on the 1995 third quarter as investors veered away from hoarding bullion, but jewellery purchases grew one percent.
"Gold demand during the first three quarters of 1996 continued to consolidate close to last year's record levels," said George Milling-Stanley, WGC manager of gold market analysis.
Consumption in the markets monitored by the WGC reached 1,942 tonnes in the first nine months, three percent below the exceptional performance recorded in the same 1995 period.

Milling-Stanley noted that investment demand last year benefited from a coincidence of positive factors, especially in Japan where investors bought 29 percent less gold in the third quarter this year.

"Among the favourable factors in Japan were a crisis of confidence in the local banking system, the Kobe earthquake encouraging people to put their savings into physical gold, and violent moves in foreign exchange rates," he said.
"There has been an adverse impact this year from investors, but investment demand is now back to a more traditional and sustainable level."
The outlook for the rest of 1996 was for further consolidation at high levels of consumption as the peak demand season is still to come in both East and West.
Significant buying was forecast from India, the world's largest gold consumer, Milling-Stanley said.
India consumed 114.1 tonnes of gold in the third quarter against 118.5 tonnes a year ago.
"India has had a leap month which is similar to a western calendar leap day which has delayed gold buying ahead of the Diwali festival of lights and the wedding season.
"It means that significant physical demand from India as well as for Ramadan and the Chinese new year will all begin in the fourth quarter," he said.
In Asian developing markets, demand was unchanged overall as higher use in the smaller economies was offset by Chinese offtake slipping six percent to 53.7 tonnes.
"Chinese demand suffered from the country's economic slowdown and customer caution -- instead of spending money on jewellery, they were putting it into savings, " Milling-Stanley said.

Gold demand in the Gulf was also lower as Saudi Arabian demand fell 16 percent to 44.3 tonnes, reflecting caution surrounding the government's policy of replacing expatriate workers with Saudi nationals.

"Uncertainties created by the latest U.S-Iraqi clash and the problems in kick-starting the Israeli-Palestinian peace process seem to be having a negative impact on consumer confidence, especially in Saudi Arabia," the WGC said.
The organisation is backed by a number of gold producers and monitors gold demand in countries accounting for about 75 percent of world gold consumption.
